paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. The page opens mid-list: this is the tail of a substituent-class enumeration that begins on an earlier printed page and carries no symbol of its own on this page, so no marker is transcribed and none is invented. Which radical symbol the list defines cannot be determined from this page alone. No paragraph numbers are printed anywhere in this patent. Three terms are broken across printed line ends by a hyphen that is part of the term itself and are rejoined here without an inserted space: 'Heteroaryl-sulfonyl-N-' + 'alkyl-amino', 'N-Alkyl-N-' + 'heteroarylaminocarbonyl', and 'Alkylcarbonyl-' + 'N-arylamino'. German 'Alkinyl' is rendered 'alkynyl' and 'Halogenalkyl' 'haloalkyl' in English, matching the convention used on earlier pages of this run. A small ink speck sits under the 'a' of 'Heterocyclylcarbonyl' on printed line 3; it is scanner dirt, not a character.

paragraphs.zh: zwei an einem gemeinsamen Kohlenstoffatom gebundene Reste R7 bilden eine Kette aus der Gruppe  OCH2CH2O und OCH2CH2CH2O, wobei diese gegebenenfalls durch ein bis vier Methylgruppen substituiert ist, oder
paragraphs.en: two radicals R7 bonded to a common carbon atom form a chain from the group  OCH2CH2O and OCH2CH2CH2O, this chain being optionally substituted by one to four methyl groups, or
paragraphs.notes: The 7 of R7 is printed as a superscript and each 2 of CH2/OCH2 as a subscript; both are transcribed inline because the field is plain text. The double space before OCH2CH2O is as printed. German 'und' is translated literally as 'and' although the sense of a chain chosen 'aus der Gruppe' is disjunctive; the reading is not resolved here. This paragraph is the preferred-embodiment counterpart of the R7 chain definition on printed page 3 (p05), and it lists only the two oxygen chains: the sulfur chains SCH2CH2S and SCH2CH2CH2S present on page 3 are absent here. That is what is printed; it is not an omission in transcription. The paragraph ends 'oder' at the foot of the page and continues on the next printed page.
